title: Anyone can make a FlowWeb login and get back in: email and password a password manager can save, a magic link, or Google, with a password reset, and every error in our own plain words
description: The Owner wants FlowWeb to be something friends can use and that can be marketed, so flowweb.app needs real logins instead of an owner-only magic link. packages/web/src/hosted/auth.ts today only sends a magic link with create_user false and shows Supabase's error text verbatim, so a crafted link can put anyone's words on the page. Give auth.ts the sign-in functions the new sign-in screens (row FW-C-081) build on, through Supabase Auth's REST API: signInWithPassword, signUp (resolves needsConfirm when the email must be confirmed first), sendLink (creates the user if new), googleUrl and signInWithGoogle, sendPasswordReset, setPassword (after a reset link lands), signOut, plus authMethods (Google only when the VITE_FW_AUTH_GOOGLE switch is on) and the hosted /v1 calls listAccounts, createAccount and acceptInvite. consumeRedirect returns { kind: 'signin' | 'recovery' | null, error } so the screens can show 'Choose a new password'. Every error a person sees comes from a closed set of our own sentences, never from the link or from Supabase's message. Accounts and roles themselves are row FW-C-083.
acceptance: authMethods is { password: true, link: true, google: false } unless VITE_FW_AUTH_GOOGLE is on, then google is true
signInWithPassword posts the email and password to /auth/v1/token?grant_type=password and keeps the session; wrong credentials throw a plain sentence that is not Supabase's text
signUp posts to /auth/v1/signup and resolves { needsConfirm: true } when no session comes back; an email already in use throws a plain sentence
sendLink posts to /auth/v1/otp with create_user true; sendPasswordReset posts to /auth/v1/recover; setPassword puts the new password to /auth/v1/user with the session's token
googleUrl() is /auth/v1/authorize?provider=google with redirect_to back to the site
consumeRedirect() answers kind 'recovery' for a reset link, 'signin' for any other sign-in link, and null with no link; an error link answers one of our sentences and never its error_description
Too many attempts (HTTP 429) throws a plain sentence
listAccounts, createAccount and acceptInvite call GET /v1/accounts, POST /v1/accounts and POST /v1/invites/<token>/accept with the session's token
signOut posts /auth/v1/logout and forgets the session
